Bertil Braun

I build and evaluate end-to-end machine-learning systems across language-model agents, scalable training infrastructure, and reinforcement learning. I work from experiments and model training through distributed systems, rigorous evaluation, and deployment. Most of my work is open source, with several projects available to try live.

Featured research system · Distributed self-play RL

AlphaZero-Style Chess & Go Engine

An end-to-end AlphaZero-style research platform that trains and serves neural chess and Go agents entirely from self-play. Performance-critical C++ implements the games, encoding, batched CUDA inference, and MCTS; Python orchestrates replay, multi-GPU DDP training, automated evaluation, and live deployment. The run below reached superhuman strength under the project’s Stockfish 13 calibration within a deliberately constrained compute envelope.

Selected work

LLM systems · Technical report

LLM-Light — Artifact-Addressed Training

A typed execution engine for building, training, and evaluating dense and MoE language models without recomputing shared work. Artifact-addressed stages provide deterministic reuse, concurrent GPU scheduling, and checkpoint recovery; the system produced the public 2.19M-example TinyPython dataset and a 42-run model sweep whose strongest configuration reached an 88.14% Python-completion pass rate.

Technical report PyTorch Dense & MoE GPT Distributed training Public dataset

LLM systems · Agents & orchestration

Agentic LLM Systems

An end-to-end agent stack for multi-agent interaction and evidence-gated software engineering, built across A2A/MCP services, model providers, retrieval stores, and durable execution. It powers a voice-first story world with five specialised agents and four tool servers, plus a coding runtime that turns tasks into tested, reviewed diffs and survives worker crashes.

Speech · Real-time systems

Voice-Light — Low-Latency Cascaded Voice Agent

A deployed full-duplex voice agent that listens and speaks concurrently, handles interruptions and backchannels, executes tools, and streams ASR, LLM, and TTS work across two GPUs. The project spans synthetic-data generation, automatic conversation labeling, two trained adapters, causal evaluation, and a measured 677 ms median from speech end to first browser audio in its final warm-system acceptance run.

Research · KIT

Scalable Automated Evaluation with LLMs

An accepted research framework for evaluating open-ended LLM output when no reference answer exists. Multiple evaluator models perform bidirectional pairwise comparisons and aggregate them into robust Elo rankings; against rankings from 20 domain experts, the strongest setting reached mean Spearman ρ = 0.83 and Kendall τ = 0.78.

Accepted paper Pairwise Elo DPO

Computer vision · Live demo

GybeLock — Windsurfing Video Intelligence

A deployed computer-vision system that turns difficult shore-shot windsurfing video into selectable, stabilised rider footage. Specialised YOLO detection and pose models feed multi-object tracking and camera stabilisation, while React, Firebase, FastAPI, and Modal carry the workflow from video upload through GPU processing to an interactive live player.

Graph RL · Technical report

Graph-Based Traffic Signal Control

A topology-flexible reinforcement-learning controller for heterogeneous urban traffic networks. Its graph policy scores road movements while deterministic incidence matrices construct each junction’s legal actions, allowing one parameter set to control networks with 41–84 junctions and 2–12 phases each; on an unseen 6×6 grid it beat max pressure at every tested demand level by 3.5–10.6 completion-rate percentage points.

Technical report Graph neural networks PPO SUMO · OpenStreetMap
